bull.b: Revenue growth and very high gross margins indicate meaningful product demand and attractive unit economics. If PEMGARDA adoption persists, these economics can provide a strong foundation for funding future commercial expansion.

Low leverage limits interest and refinancing pressure, giving Invivyd greater flexibility while it funds clinical programs and commercial infrastructure. This is particularly valuable for a biotechnology company with volatile development timelines.

Demonstrated activity across evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants supports the company’s engineered-antibody strategy, while expansion into other infectious diseases broadens the potential addressable market and reduces reliance on a single pathogen.

bear.b: Large recurring losses and negative operating cash flow mean the business is not yet self-funding. Continued clinical and commercial investment may require additional external capital, creating dilution and execution risk if profitability remains delayed.

The end of the EUA creates a durable regulatory dependency over the next several months. Continued product access and revenue growth will depend on securing a clear approval pathway, FDA review and successful conversion of existing data.

A shrinking or less predictable COVID prevention market can constrain PEMGARDA growth and reduce the commercial opportunity for follow-on products. Lower utilization also increases the importance of expanding into additional infectious-disease indications.
